column1: af|Not a conventional colony. Britain constrained Afghan foreign relations after 1879; Afghanistan regained full control in 1919. The Soviet invasion and military occupation lasted 1979–1989.
al|Ottoman rule covered most of the area from the late 1400s to independence in 1912. Italy occupied Albania in 1939–1943, followed by Nazi Germany in 1943–1944.
dz|France conquered Algiers in 1830 and expanded control inland over the following decades. French colonial rule ended with independence in 1962, after an eight-year war.

ad|A special case: joint lordship began in 1278. French and Spanish-linked co-princes governed under the old arrangement until the 1993 constitution established parliamentary democracy; the co-princes remain heads of state.
ao|Portuguese colonial expansion began with coastal settlements in the 1500s, including Luanda in 1575. Control over the interior came much later. Angola became independent in 1975.
ag|English settlement began in 1632. British colonial rule, interrupted briefly by France in 1666–1667, ended with independence in 1981.
ar|Spain colonised parts of the region from the 1500s. The Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata existed from 1776; revolution began in 1810 and independence was declared in 1816.
am|Russian imperial expansion brought eastern Armenian territories under its rule in the early 1800s. After independence in 1918–1920, Soviet rule began in 1920 and ended in 1991.

au|British colonisation began in 1788, displacing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples. Federation created a self-governing Commonwealth in 1901; legal independence developed in stages, culminating in the Australia Acts of 1986.
at|Nazi Germany annexed Austria in 1938 and ruled until 1945. Allied occupation then lasted from 1945 to 1955, when a state treaty restored full sovereignty.
az|The Russian Empire absorbed the area in the early 1800s. Independence in 1918–1920 was followed by Soviet rule from 1920 to 1991.
bs|English settlers arrived in 1648; formal royal colonial government began in 1718. Following a brief Spanish occupation in 1782–1783, British rule continued until independence in 1973.
bh|British protection developed through nineteenth-century treaties, especially the agreement of 1861. It ended with independence in 1971; the local Al Khalifa dynasty remained in power.
bd|Bengal came under British East India Company control after 1757 and later British Crown rule. From 1947 to 1971, the area was East Pakistan; Bangladesh became independent in 1971.
bb|English settlement began in 1627. The island remained under British colonial rule until independence in 1966, and became a republic in 2021.

by|Much of present-day Belarus passed from the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth to Russia in the partitions of 1772–1795. Soviet rule followed the revolutionary era; Nazi occupation interrupted it in 1941–1944. Independence came in 1991.

be|The territory passed through Spanish and Austrian Habsburg rule before French annexation in 1795–1814 and union with the Netherlands in 1815–1830. Belgium became independent in 1830; German occupations followed in 1914–1918 and 1940–1944.
bz|British settlement developed from the 1600s. British Honduras became a crown colony in 1862 and achieved independence as Belize in 1981.
bj|France conquered the Kingdom of Dahomey in the 1890s and established colonial rule. Independence came in 1960; the country adopted the name Benin in 1975.
bt|Bhutan was not formally colonised. A 1910 treaty gave Britain influence over external affairs until 1947; a related arrangement with independent India began in 1949 and was revised in 2007.
bo|Spanish conquest began in the 1530s. The colonial region known as Upper Peru became independent as Bolivia in 1825.

ba|Ottoman conquest began in 1463. Austria-Hungary administered Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1878 and annexed it in 1908; that rule ended in 1918. It later formed part of Yugoslavia until independence in 1992.
bw|Britain established the Bechuanaland Protectorate in 1885. Protectorate status ended with independence as Botswana in 1966.
br|Portuguese colonisation followed the arrival of 1500. Brazil declared independence in 1822 and initially remained a monarchy under a branch of the Portuguese royal family.
bn|Brunei became a British protectorate in 1888. Japanese occupation interrupted this in 1941–1945; full independence came in 1984 while the sultanate continued.
bg|Ottoman conquest was completed in the late 1300s. Bulgaria gained autonomy in 1878 and declared full independence in 1908. Soviet troops occupied the country in 1944–1947.

bf|French conquest in the late 1890s brought the territory into its colonial empire. Upper Volta was constituted as a colony in 1919, later reorganised, and became independent in 1960; it was renamed Burkina Faso in 1984.

bi|German colonial rule was established in the 1890s. Belgium occupied the area in 1916 and later administered Ruanda-Urundi under international mandates and trusteeship. Burundi became independent in 1962.
kh|Cambodia was a French protectorate from 1863 to 1953. Japanese influence and occupation disrupted French control in 1941–1945. Vietnamese military intervention and troop presence lasted 1978–1989.

cm|Germany established Kamerun in 1884; its rule ended during World War I in 1916. France and Britain then administered separate territories. French Cameroon became independent in 1960, joined by British Southern Cameroons in 1961.

ca|French colonisation began in the early 1600s; Britain acquired most of New France in 1763. Confederation in 1867 created a self-governing dominion. Legislative autonomy followed in 1931, and constitutional patriation in 1982.
cv|Portuguese settlement began in the 1460s on previously uninhabited islands. Colonial rule ended with Cabo Verde’s independence in 1975.
cf|France established control in the late 1800s, organising Ubangi-Shari as a territory in 1903. The Central African Republic became independent in 1960.
td|French conquest began around 1900; Chad became a separate colony in 1920. French colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.
cl|Spanish conquest and settlement began in the 1540s, though Indigenous resistance limited control in the south. The independence process began in 1810, with independence proclaimed in 1818.

cn|China was itself an imperial power. The Mongol-led Yuan dynasty ruled in 1271–1368 and the Manchu-led Qing in 1644–1912. Foreign concessions and Japanese occupations affected parts of China in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries; China as a whole was not one European colony.
co|Spain conquered and colonised the region in the 1500s. Independence struggles began in 1810; the 1819 victory at Boyacá helped secure independence and the creation of Gran Colombia.

km|French control began with Mayotte in 1841 and expanded through protectorates over other islands in 1886. Comoros declared independence in 1975. Mayotte remained under French administration, a status Comoros disputes.
cr|Spanish colonisation developed in the 1500s. Costa Rica declared independence from Spain in 1821, later leaving the Central American federation in 1838.

hr|Croatian lands experienced different Hungarian, Habsburg, Venetian and Ottoman rulers over centuries. Habsburg rule over much of the territory lasted 1527–1918. Croatia was later part of Yugoslavia until independence in 1991.
cu|Spanish colonial rule began in 1511 and ended in 1898. A US military occupation followed in 1898–1902; Cuba became formally independent in 1902, with another US occupation in 1906–1909.

cy|Ottoman rule lasted 1571–1878. Britain administered Cyprus from 1878 and formally annexed it in 1914. Independence came in 1960. The island has been divided since the Turkish military intervention of 1974.

cz|The Czech lands were under Habsburg rule from 1526 to 1918. Nazi Germany occupied the Czech lands in 1938–1945, with the Protectorate established in 1939. Czechoslovakia split peacefully into Czechia and Slovakia in 1993.
ci|France declared Côte d’Ivoire a colony in 1893 after earlier coastal treaties and settlements. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.
cd|The Congo Free State was controlled personally by Belgium’s King Leopold II from 1885 to 1908. Belgium then governed the Belgian Congo from 1908 until independence in 1960.
dk|Denmark was a regional kingdom and colonial power, rather than a modern overseas colony. Nazi Germany occupied it from 1940 to 1945.
dj|French footholds began with treaties in 1862; French Somaliland was established in 1896. Renamed the French Territory of the Afars and Issas in 1967, it became independent as Djibouti in 1977.

dm|France established colonial settlements in the 1600s and Britain obtained Dominica in 1763. After further conflict and a French occupation in 1778–1784, British rule continued until independence in 1978.

do|Spain colonised Hispaniola from 1493. The eastern part passed through French control in 1795–1809, returned to Spain until 1821, and came under Haiti in 1822–1844. Independence was declared in 1844; Spain briefly reannexed it in 1861–1865 and the US occupied it in 1916–1924.
ec|Spanish conquest began in 1534. Victory over Spanish forces in 1822 brought the territory into Gran Colombia; Ecuador became a separate republic in 1830.

eg|Ottoman rule began in 1517, with increasing local autonomy later. Britain occupied Egypt in 1882 and imposed a formal protectorate in 1914–1922. Independence in 1922 was limited; British forces left the Suez Canal zone in 1956.
sv|Spain conquered the region in the 1520s. Independence from Spain came in 1821; El Salvador later left the Central American federation in 1839.
gq|Portugal ceded its claims to Spain in 1778. Spanish colonial control developed unevenly over the islands and mainland and ended with independence in 1968.

er|Italy established the colony of Eritrea in 1890 and lost it in 1941. British administration lasted 1941–1952, followed by federation with Ethiopia in 1952–1962 and Ethiopian annexation in 1962–1991. Formal independence came in 1993.

ee|Swedish and Russian rule followed earlier Danish and German control; the Russian Empire governed from 1721 to 1918. Soviet occupation in 1940–1941 was followed by Nazi occupation in 1941–1944 and renewed Soviet rule in 1944–1991.
sz|British administration lasted from 1903 until independence in 1968. Previously known internationally as Swaziland, the kingdom adopted the name Eswatini in 2018.
et|Ethiopia retained independence during most of Africa’s colonial era, defeating Italy at Adwa in 1896. Italy nevertheless invaded and occupied it from 1936 to 1941.
fj|Fiji was ceded to Britain in 1874. British colonial rule ended with independence in 1970.
fi|Swedish rule developed during the medieval period and lasted until 1809. Finland then became an autonomous grand duchy under Russia from 1809 until independence in 1917.

fr|France was a major imperial power, rather than a modern overseas colony. Nazi Germany occupied much of it in 1940–1944; Vichy governed the initially unoccupied zone until German forces entered it in 1942.
ga|French footholds began with coastal treaties in 1839–1841. Colonial control expanded in the later 1800s; Gabon became independent in 1960.
gm|British colonial claims began in 1664, with later changes in boundaries and administration. The modern colony and protectorate became independent as The Gambia in 1965.
ge|The Russian Empire began annexing Georgian kingdoms in 1801. Independence in 1918–1921 was followed by Soviet conquest in 1921 and Soviet rule until 1991.

de|After Nazi Germany’s defeat, the US, UK, France and USSR occupied separate zones from 1945. Two German states formed in 1949; occupation arrangements changed in 1955, and the remaining Four-Power rights were suspended at reunification in 1990 and formally ended in 1991.
gh|Britain established the Gold Coast colony in 1874 and later extended control over Asante and the north. The Gold Coast and British Togoland became independent as Ghana in 1957.

gr|Ottoman conquest spread across much of Greece in the 1400s. The independence war began in 1821; an independent Greek state was recognised in 1830, with later territorial additions. Axis occupation lasted 1941–1944.
gd|French settlement began in 1649. Britain acquired Grenada in 1763, lost it to France in 1779, and regained it in 1783. British rule ended with independence in 1974.
gt|Spanish conquest began in 1524. Guatemala declared independence from Spain in 1821 and subsequently belonged to a Central American federation before becoming a separate republic.
gn|French colonial control expanded in the late 1800s; French Guinea became a colony in 1891. Guinea voted to leave the French colonial system and became independent in 1958.
gw|Portuguese trading posts appeared in the 1400s, but conquest of the interior came much later. Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973, recognised by Portugal in 1974.
gy|Dutch colonies developed in the 1600s. Britain took control in the early 1800s, confirmed in 1814; British Guiana was consolidated in 1831. Independence came in 1966.

ht|France obtained the western part of Hispaniola from Spain in 1697. The Haitian Revolution began in 1791 and ended French colonial rule with independence in 1804. The US occupied Haiti in 1915–1934.

hn|Spanish conquest developed from the 1520s. Independence from Spain came in 1821; Honduras left the Central American federation in 1838. British influence and claims affected the Caribbean coast separately.

hu|Following the Ottoman victory in 1526, Hungary was divided between Ottoman, Habsburg and Transylvanian domains. Ottoman control in the centre lasted mainly 1541–1699; Habsburg rule continued until 1918. Germany occupied Hungary in 1944, followed by Soviet military domination after 1945.

is|Iceland came under Norway in 1262–1264 and later the Danish crown. It became a sovereign kingdom in union with Denmark in 1918 and a republic in 1944. British and then US forces were stationed there during World War II.

in|Many regional kingdoms and empires preceded British expansion. East India Company control grew after 1757; direct British Crown rule lasted 1858–1947. Independence and partition came in 1947; princely states followed different arrangements.

id|Dutch control developed gradually from the 1600s and never began everywhere at once. Japan occupied the islands in 1942–1945. Independence was proclaimed in 1945 and recognised by the Netherlands in 1949; western New Guinea followed a separate later process.

ir|Iran was itself a centre of empires, rather than a single modern European colony. Arab conquest occurred in the seventh century and Mongol conquest in the thirteenth. Britain and the USSR jointly occupied parts of Iran in 1941–1946.

iq|Ottoman rule covered much of the region from the 1500s until World War I. British occupation began during the war and a mandate followed in 1920; formal independence came in 1932. The US-led occupation authority governed in 2003–2004.

ie|English intervention began in 1169 and control expanded over centuries. The island was incorporated into the United Kingdom in 1801. Most of Ireland became the Irish Free State in 1922; Northern Ireland remained in the UK.

il|The territory was under Ottoman rule in 1517–1917. British military administration followed, then the British Mandate in 1923–1948. Israel declared independence in 1948. These dates describe rule over the territory before the modern state.

it|Before unification in 1861, the peninsula contained many states under different local and foreign rulers, including Spanish and Austrian dynasties. Nazi Germany occupied much of northern and central Italy in 1943–1945.
jm|Spanish colonial rule began in 1509. England seized Jamaica in 1655, and British rule continued until independence in 1962.
jp|Japan was not a European colony and became an imperial power itself. After defeat in World War II, an Allied occupation led by the US lasted from 1945 to 1952; some islands returned later.
jo|The territory was under Ottoman rule from 1516 until 1918. The Emirate of Transjordan was established under British supervision in 1921 and became independent in 1946.

kz|Russian imperial control expanded across the steppe from the 1700s through the 1800s. Soviet rule followed the revolutionary era; Kazakhstan was a union republic from 1936 until independence in 1991.
ke|Britain established the East Africa Protectorate in 1895 and the Kenya colony in 1920. British rule ended with independence in 1963; earlier coastal history included Portuguese and Omani rule.
ki|The Gilbert Islands became a British protectorate in 1892 and part of a colony in 1916. Japan occupied some islands in 1941–1943. Kiribati became independent in 1979.
kw|Kuwait was under British protection from 1899 to 1961, with local rulers retaining internal authority. Iraq invaded and occupied it from August 1990 until liberation in February 1991.
kg|Russian imperial conquest incorporated the territory during the 1800s. Soviet administration followed; Kyrgyzstan became a union republic in 1936 and independent in 1991.
la|Laos was under French colonial rule from 1893 to 1953. Japanese intervention briefly displaced French power in 1945; the independence process then continued after the war.

lv|Latvian territories passed through German, Polish–Lithuanian and Swedish control before incorporation into Russia during the 1700s. Independence in 1918 was followed by Soviet occupation in 1940–1941, Nazi occupation in 1941–1944/1945, and Soviet rule until 1991.

lb|Ottoman rule lasted from 1516 until 1918. France established Greater Lebanon in 1920 and administered it under a mandate. Independence was declared in 1943; the last French troops withdrew in 1946.
ls|Basutoland became a British protectorate in 1868. It was administered by the Cape Colony in 1871–1884, then directly by Britain until independence as Lesotho in 1966.

lr|Liberia was founded through settlement sponsored by the American Colonization Society from 1822 and declared independence in 1847. It was not a US government colony; settler domination of Indigenous communities remained an important part of its history.

ly|Ottoman rule began in 1551 and ended with the Italian invasion in 1911. Italian colonial control lasted until defeat in 1943. British and French administrations governed different areas until independence in 1951.

li|The principality was created within the Holy Roman Empire in 1719 and became sovereign when that empire dissolved in 1806. It was not a modern overseas colony; close customs and diplomatic relationships with Austria and Switzerland did not make it part of those countries.

lt|Most of Lithuania was incorporated into Russia in 1795. Independence returned in 1918. Soviet occupation in 1940–1941 was followed by Nazi occupation in 1941–1944 and renewed Soviet rule until restoration of independence in 1990–1991.

lu|Luxembourg passed through Burgundian, Spanish, Austrian and French rule. From 1815 to 1890 it shared a monarch with the Netherlands while developing separate statehood. Germany occupied it in 1914–1918 and 1940–1944.
mg|France invaded in 1895 and annexed Madagascar in 1896. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.
mw|Britain proclaimed a protectorate in 1891, later named Nyasaland. It belonged to the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland in 1953–1963 and became independent as Malawi in 1964.

my|Different territories had different rulers: Britain acquired Penang in 1786 and progressively expanded control over Malaya and northern Borneo. Japanese occupation lasted 1941/1942–1945. Malaya became independent in 1957; Malaysia formed in 1963.
mv|The Maldives was a British protectorate from 1887 until independence in 1965. Local sultans retained internal authority; a republic replaced the sultanate in 1968.

ml|French conquest developed in the late 1800s; much of the territory was administered as French Sudan. Independence came through the Mali Federation in 1960, followed that year by the separate Republic of Mali.
mt|The Knights of St John ruled Malta in 1530–1798. French occupation lasted 1798–1800, followed by British control from 1800 until independence in 1964.

mh|Germany established a protectorate in 1885. Japan took control in 1914, followed by the US in 1944. US-administered UN trusteeship began in 1947; free association took effect in 1986 and trusteeship formally ended in 1990.
mr|French control developed from the early 1900s; Mauritania became a colony in 1920. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.
mu|Dutch settlement lasted intermittently from 1638 to 1710. France took possession in 1715; Britain captured the island in 1810 and ruled until independence in 1968.
mx|Spanish conquest of the Aztec capital in 1521 began the colonial era of New Spain. Independence came in 1821. A French intervention supported a short-lived empire in 1862–1867.

fm|Spain claimed the Caroline Islands and sold them to Germany in 1899. Japan took control in 1914; US control followed during World War II. A US-administered trusteeship began in 1947; free association took effect in 1986 and trusteeship ended in 1990.

md|Much of present-day Moldova, then Bessarabia, passed from Ottoman-linked Moldavia to Russia in 1812. It united with Romania in 1918, was taken by the USSR in 1940, occupied by Romania in 1941–1944, and returned to Soviet rule until 1991.

mc|The Grimaldi family established rule in 1297, with interruptions. Monaco was annexed by France in 1793–1814 and under Sardinian protection in 1815–1861. A treaty recognised its sovereignty in 1861.

mn|Qing rule over Outer Mongolia developed from 1691 and ended with the independence declaration of 1911. Chinese forces reoccupied it in 1919–1921. Later Soviet influence was extensive, but Mongolia was not a Soviet republic.

me|Montenegro maintained varying degrees of autonomy while neighbouring territories were under Ottoman rule. Independence was internationally recognised in 1878. It joined the Yugoslav state in 1918 and restored separate independence in 2006.

ma|Most of Morocco was a French protectorate from 1912 to 1956, with separate Spanish zones and an international zone at Tangier. Independence was restored in 1956; some territorial questions followed different timelines.
mz|Portuguese coastal footholds began around 1500, with inland colonial control expanding much later. Portuguese rule ended with independence in 1975.
mm|Britain conquered Burma in stages in 1824–1885 and annexed the remaining kingdom in 1886. Japanese occupation lasted 1942–1945. Independence from Britain came in 1948.

na|Germany established South West Africa in 1884. South Africa occupied it in 1915 and later administered it under a mandate, continuing after that mandate was revoked. Namibia became independent in 1990.
nr|Germany annexed Nauru in 1888. Australian-led administration began in 1914, later under international mandates and trusteeship. Japan occupied it in 1942–1945. Independence came in 1968.

np|Nepal was not formally colonised by a European power. The Anglo-Nepalese War of 1814–1816 ended with territorial losses and British influence; a 1923 treaty explicitly recognised Nepal’s independence.

nl|Habsburg rule in the 1500s led to revolt against Spain from 1568. The northern provinces declared separation in 1581, recognised in 1648. French control lasted 1795–1813; Nazi occupation lasted 1940–1945.

nz|British sovereignty was asserted in 1840 following the Treaty of Waitangi, whose interpretation remains contested. Dominion status came in 1907; legislative autonomy followed in 1947. Māori communities experienced substantial dispossession during colonisation.

ni|Spanish conquest began in the 1520s. Independence from Spain came in 1821; Nicaragua left the Central American federation in 1838. US military occupations occurred in 1912–1925 and 1926–1933, while the Caribbean coast had a separate British-influenced history.
ne|French military conquest expanded around 1900 and Niger became a colony in 1922. Colonial rule ended with independence in 1960.
ng|Britain annexed Lagos in 1861 and gradually expanded control. The northern and southern protectorates were amalgamated in 1914; Nigeria became independent in 1960.
kp|Japan colonised Korea from 1910 to 1945. Soviet forces occupied the northern half in 1945–1948; North Korea was established as a separate state in 1948.
mk|Ottoman rule covered the area from the late 1300s until 1912. It then came under Serbian rule and later Yugoslavia, with wartime occupations interrupting that period. Independence came in 1991.
no|Norway shared a crown with Denmark from 1380 until 1814, then with Sweden from 1814 to 1905. Nazi Germany occupied Norway from 1940 to 1945.
om|Portugal controlled Muscat and other coastal strongholds in 1507–1650. Oman later became an imperial power itself. British influence was substantial, but Oman was not formally a British colony.

pk|The territories of present-day Pakistan came under British control at different times: Sindh in 1843 and Punjab in 1849, with other areas following different arrangements. Pakistan became independent with the partition of British India in 1947.

pw|Spain controlled Palau in the late 1800s and sold it to Germany in 1899. Japan took control in 1914; US administration followed World War II under a UN trusteeship from 1947. Independence in free association with the US came in 1994.

ps|Ottoman rule lasted 1516/1517–1917/1918, followed by British administration and the mandate until 1948. Jordan controlled the West Bank and Egypt administered Gaza in 1948–1967. Israel occupied both in 1967. Palestinian self-government began in the 1990s; occupation and sovereignty remain unresolved, with Gaza’s status after Israel’s 2005 withdrawal disputed by Israel and international bodies.

pa|Spain colonised the isthmus from the early 1500s to 1821. Panama then joined Gran Colombia and remained linked to Colombia until 1903. The US administered the Canal Zone in 1903–1979; full control of the canal transferred in 1999.

pg|Germany and Britain divided eastern New Guinea in 1884. Australian administration developed from 1906 and expanded after Germany’s defeat in 1914, with Japanese occupation of parts during World War II. Papua New Guinea became independent in 1975.
py|Spanish settlement began with Asunción in 1537. Paraguay became independent from Spain in 1811.
pe|Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire began in 1532. Independence was declared in 1821 and secured through major military victories in 1824; the last mainland Spanish stronghold surrendered in 1826.
ph|Spanish colonial rule developed from 1565 to 1898. US rule followed in 1898–1946, interrupted by Japanese occupation in 1942–1945. Full independence was recognised in 1946.

pl|Partitions in 1772, 1793 and 1795 divided Poland among Russia, Prussia and Austria; it regained independence in 1918. Nazi Germany and the USSR invaded in 1939. German occupation ended in 1945, followed by a Soviet-dominated political order until 1989.

pt|Portugal became an independent kingdom in the 1100s and later a colonial power. It shared the Spanish monarch under the Iberian Union in 1580–1640. French invasions and occupation affected it in 1807–1811.
qa|Ottoman forces were present from 1871 to 1915. Qatar became a British protectorate in 1916 and gained independence in 1971, with the local ruling dynasty continuing.
cg|France established colonial control through treaties and expansion from 1880. The territory became part of French Equatorial Africa and gained independence as the Republic of the Congo in 1960.

ro|Wallachia and Moldavia were under varying Ottoman suzerainty for centuries; they united in 1859. Independence was proclaimed in 1877 and recognised in 1878. Transylvania had a different Habsburg and Hungarian history before joining Romania in 1918.

ru|Medieval Rus’ principalities came under Mongol conquest in the 1230s–1240s and paid tribute to the Golden Horde. Moscow’s final break with that domination is conventionally dated to 1480. Russia later became an imperial power itself.
rw|Germany established colonial control in the 1890s. Belgium occupied Rwanda in 1916 and later administered it under mandate and trusteeship until independence in 1962.
kn|English and French settlers divided Saint Kitts during the 1600s. Britain obtained full control in 1713. British rule over the federation ended with independence in 1983.
lc|France and Britain repeatedly contested Saint Lucia in the 1600s–1700s. Britain finally secured it in 1814 and ruled until independence in 1979.
vc|French settlement began in 1719 after prolonged Indigenous resistance. Britain obtained the island in 1763; France retook it in 1779, and Britain regained it in 1783. Independence came in 1979.

ws|Germany ruled western Samoa from 1900 to 1914. New Zealand then occupied and administered it, later under mandate and trusteeship, until independence in 1962. American Samoa followed a separate history.

sm|San Marino preserved a long tradition of independent republican government rather than a sustained colonial period. Brief occupations included Cesare Borgia in 1503 and Cardinal Alberoni in 1739; German and Allied forces entered during fighting in 1944.

sa|Parts of today’s Saudi Arabia, particularly the Hejaz, were under Ottoman rule from 1517 to 1916, with interruptions and varying control. The modern kingdom was unified in 1932; the entire present territory was never one European colony.
sn|France established a settlement at Saint-Louis in 1659 and later expanded colonial control inland. Senegal became independent in 1960, initially as part of the short-lived Mali Federation.

rs|Ottoman conquest culminated in the fall of the Serbian despotate in 1459. Autonomy developed after nineteenth-century uprisings; independence was internationally recognised in 1878. Serbia later formed part of Yugoslavia and became a separate state in 2006.
sc|France claimed the Seychelles in 1756 and settlement began in 1770. Britain took control during the Napoleonic era, formalised in 1814. Independence came in 1976.
sl|British-sponsored settlement at Freetown began in 1787. The coastal colony was established in 1808 and an inland protectorate in 1896. Both became independent as Sierra Leone in 1961.

sg|A British trading settlement began in 1819; Singapore became a crown colony in 1867. Japanese occupation lasted 1942–1945. It gained self-government in 1959, joined Malaysia in 1963 and became independent in 1965.

sk|Most Slovak territory formed part of the Kingdom of Hungary for centuries, later within the Habsburg monarchy until 1918. A German-aligned Slovak state existed in 1939–1945, with German occupation from 1944. Slovakia became separate from Czechoslovakia in 1993.

si|Slovene lands were largely within Habsburg domains for centuries until 1918, with a French interruption in parts in 1809–1813. Axis powers divided and occupied the territory in 1941–1945. Slovenia left Yugoslavia in 1991.
sb|Britain established a protectorate over the southern islands in 1893, with further islands added later. Japan occupied parts in 1942–1945. Independence came in 1978.

so|British and Italian colonial rule developed in the late 1800s in different parts of present-day Somalia. British Somaliland and the Italian-administered UN trust territory became independent and united in 1960; French Somaliland later became Djibouti separately.

za|Dutch settlement at the Cape began in 1652. British control developed from 1795 and permanently from 1806, expanding after wars with African kingdoms and Boer republics. The Union formed in 1910; legislative independence followed in 1931. Apartheid ended with democratic elections in 1994.
kr|Japan colonised Korea from 1910 to 1945. A US military government administered the southern half in 1945–1948; the Republic of Korea was established in 1948.

ss|The south was incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan condominium from 1899 to 1956, following earlier Egyptian expansion. It then formed part of independent Sudan until South Sudan became independent in 2011.

es|Roman rule covered much of the peninsula in antiquity. Muslim-ruled states controlled varying areas from 711 to 1492, alongside expanding Christian kingdoms. Napoleonic French occupation affected Spain in 1808–1814; modern Spain was itself a colonial power.

lk|Portugal controlled coastal areas from the 1500s until displacement by the Dutch in 1658. Britain took Dutch territories in 1796 and conquered the Kandyan kingdom in 1815. British rule ended with independence in 1948.
sd|Turco-Egyptian conquest began in 1820–1821, followed by the independent Mahdist state in 1885–1898. Anglo-Egyptian condominium rule lasted from 1899 until independence in 1956.

sr|English colonisation developed in the 1600s; the Dutch took control in 1667. British occupations interrupted Dutch rule in 1799–1802 and 1804–1816. Suriname became independent from the Netherlands in 1975.

se|Sweden belonged to the Kalmar Union from 1397, with repeated interruptions and contests over Danish-led rule, until 1523. It subsequently became a regional imperial power and was not a modern overseas colony.

ch|The Swiss Confederation developed from the late 1200s and gradually escaped Habsburg and imperial authority. Independence from the Holy Roman Empire was formally recognised in 1648. French invasion imposed the Helvetic Republic in 1798–1803.
sy|Ottoman rule lasted from 1516 until 1918. France established control in 1920 and governed under a mandate. Independence developed during World War II; the last French troops left in 1946.
st|Portuguese settlement of the previously uninhabited islands began in the late 1400s. The plantation colony became independent in 1975.

tj|Russian conquest brought parts of the territory under direct rule in the late 1800s; other areas belonged to the Russian-protected Emirate of Bukhara. Soviet control followed in the 1920s. Tajikistan became a union republic in 1929 and independent in 1991.

tz|Germany controlled mainland Tanganyika from the 1880s until World War I; British administration followed until independence in 1961. Zanzibar was an Omani-linked sultanate and British protectorate in 1890–1963. The two united in 1964.

th|Thailand was never formally colonised by a European power. It negotiated concessions and lost territories while retaining sovereignty. Japan invaded in December 1941, then maintained troops under an alliance arrangement until 1945.

tl|Portuguese colonial influence began in the 1500s. Japan occupied the territory in 1942–1945. After a brief independence declaration in 1975, Indonesia invaded and occupied it until 1999. UN transitional administration lasted 1999–2002, when independence was restored.

tg|Germany established Togoland in 1884 and lost control in 1914. Britain and France administered separate mandates. French Togoland became independent as Togo in 1960; British Togoland joined what became Ghana in 1957.
to|Tonga retained its indigenous monarchy and was not formally annexed as a colony. It was a British protected state from 1900 to 1970, when full control of external affairs returned.

tt|Spain colonised Trinidad from the late 1500s; Britain captured it in 1797. Tobago changed European rulers repeatedly before becoming British definitively in 1814. The islands were united administratively in 1889 and became independent in 1962.
tn|Ottoman rule began in 1574, later with substantial autonomy under local beys. France imposed a protectorate in 1881, which ended with independence in 1956.
tm|Russian conquest in the 1880s incorporated most of the territory into the empire. Soviet rule followed; Turkmenistan became a union republic in 1924 and independent in 1991.

tr|Modern Türkiye emerged from the Ottoman Empire, itself a major imperial power. Allied occupation affected parts of the former empire in 1918–1923, including Istanbul; the republic was proclaimed in 1923 after the independence war.
tv|The Ellice Islands became a British protectorate in 1892 and part of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony in 1916. They separated as Tuvalu in 1975–1976 and became independent in 1978.
ug|Britain declared the Uganda Protectorate in 1894, expanding its boundaries over subsequent years. Protectorate rule ended with independence in 1962.

ua|Different Ukrainian regions experienced Polish–Lithuanian, Russian, Habsburg and other rule. Most became part of the USSR in 1922; Nazi occupation affected the territory in 1941–1944. Independence came in 1991. Russia has occupied Crimea and parts of the east since 2014 and launched a full-scale invasion in 2022; those territories remain internationally recognised as Ukrainian.

ae|The Trucial States entered maritime treaties with Britain from 1820 and exclusive protection agreements in 1892. The protected relationship ended in 1971, when the UAE formed; Ras Al Khaimah joined in 1972.

gb|The modern UK formed through unions of kingdoms and became a major colonial power. Earlier foreign conquests affected its constituent territories: Rome ruled much of Britain in 43–410 CE, and the Norman conquest of England began in 1066. The whole modern UK was not a later overseas colony.

us|European powers colonised different regions from the 1500s onward. The thirteen British colonies declared independence in 1776, recognised in 1783. Later US expansion incorporated territories with distinct Indigenous, Spanish, French, Mexican and other histories.

uy|Spain and Portugal contested the region from the colonial era. Portuguese forces invaded in 1816, followed by incorporation into Brazil in 1822. Uruguay’s independence was recognised in 1828 after war and diplomacy.

uz|Russian imperial conquest brought much of the region under control in the 1860s–1870s, while Bukhara and Khiva became protectorates. Soviet rule followed in the 1920s; Uzbekistan was a union republic from 1924 until independence in 1991.
vu|France and Britain jointly administered the New Hebrides as a condominium from 1906. This unusual dual colonial system ended with independence as Vanuatu in 1980.

va|The modern Vatican City State was created by the Lateran Treaty in 1929. Earlier papal territories were absorbed into Italy, with Rome taken in 1870. Vatican City’s history is therefore different from a conventional colony gaining independence.
ve|Spanish colonisation began in the early 1500s. Independence was declared in 1811 and secured through the independence wars; Venezuela became a separate state from Gran Colombia in 1830.

vn|French conquest began in 1858 and control over Vietnam was consolidated in the 1880s. Japanese occupation and influence lasted 1940–1945. Independence was declared in 1945; French rule ended after war in 1954. The country was divided until reunification in 1976.

ye|Northern Yemen experienced Ottoman rule in two periods, principally 1538–1635 and 1849–1918. Britain controlled Aden from 1839 and later protected surrounding southern territories until 1967. North and South Yemen united in 1990.
zm|British South Africa Company control expanded in the 1890s. Northern Rhodesia came under direct British colonial administration in 1924 and became independent as Zambia in 1964.

zw|British South Africa Company rule began in 1890. Southern Rhodesia became a self-governing British colony in 1923. A white-minority government unilaterally declared independence in 1965, without international recognition; recognised independence as Zimbabwe came in 1980.
